lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The ice is quiet, and that's the point in Toronto right now - no games, no noise, just the hard work of sorting out what this roster really is. The biggest fresh note is the hire of Andy O'Brien to run sport performance, a telling move in a summer that has already brought major churn and a deeper bet on health, conditioning and recovery. The Maple Leafs sit in the deep offseason after a year that forced a reset, and the focus now is less on slogans than on fit. Auston Matthews' recovery remains the storyline that still bends the whole picture, while the prospect ladder gets a little more interesting with Juuso Ainasto at No. 18. What matters next is camp: who arrives ready, who sticks, and whether the new staff can turn all this reshuffling into a cleaner roster by September.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The summer headline in Toronto is not a box score - it's a roster shakeup with teeth. The Blue Jays placed Trey Yesavage on the 15-day injured list, a move that immediately shadows the club's pitching depth and its plans for the next stretch of the offseason. Toronto is 0-0 in the current season phase, because the real work now is construction, not chasing games. The front office has already shown its hand, stocking the bullpen and shuffling the 40-man while the calendar turns toward camp. Yesavage's absence puts even more weight on the arms the Jays just added and the ones still fighting for innings. What matters next is whether Toronto keeps adding protection for a staff that suddenly looks thinner than it did yesterday.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: Quiet is the sound of August in Toronto - but the silence has a little steel in it. The Raptors added two champions in Trey Jemison III and Andre Jackson Jr., the kind of end-of-rotation moves that tell you the front office is still sanding the edges of the roster while bigger questions hang over the board. The club finished 46-36 and fifth in the East, and that record now reads like a prompt, not a verdict: how much of this core stays intact, and who is worth the next bet? Jakob Poeltl's $84 million deal looms over the Sabonis story, a blunt reminder that one contract can kill a swing. What comes next is camp competition - and whether Toronto keeps shopping for a cleaner fit or doubles down on continuity.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The camp mood in Ashburn has changed in a hurry - less about merely sorting a roster, more about finding the right gear for Jayden Daniels. Stefon Diggs' arrival has jolted the receiver room and given Washington a true No. 2 behind Terry McLaurin, while the young pass-catchers now fight for scraps and roles alike. The Commanders are in training camp, and the depth chart is still being hammered into shape: Diggs, Luke McCaffrey, Jaylin Lane and Antonio Williams all have something to prove, while Dyami Brown's return and the punter shakeup after Tress Way's pectoral injury add to the churn. Trey Amos is on the physically unable to perform list as a precaution, but should be back soon. What matters next is simple: how quickly Diggs and Daniels build timing when the pads stay on and the preseason lights come up.

article.title: Thursday's Skate
paragraphs: The Leafs are deep into an offseason rebuild, with reports pointing to a crowded forward picture and little room for Semyon Der-Arguchintsev, while prospect watch continues to center on Juuso Ainasto and the No. 1 pick Gavin McKenna from the broader summer overhaul.

The Blue Jays have a timely offensive note after a 5-4 win over the Astros, with Guerrero Jr. resting, and the Raptors are still shaping their roster after adding an NCAA champion in their latest signing. For the Commanders, camp notes from Week 2 have highlighted standouts and a bold Stefon Diggs addition has already produced winners and losers in early evaluations.
